title: Fine

sourceCredit: Fred Johnson · The Moth, “A Hard Truth”
imagePrompt: Create one 1536 x 1024 pixel painted scene sheet, EXACTLY TWO COLUMNS BY THREE ROWS, six equal-width WIDE cinematic panels in row-major order 0 to 5. Each column is 768 pixels; rows are approximately 341, 341 and 342 pixels high. Hard straight cell edges; no gutters, no panel labels, no numbers, no captions, no typography, no readable lettering, no logos. Every cell is its own complete environment, never a sprite or a cutout. Use the polished watercolor and fine ink on textured cream paper style of Enough: warm directional light, deep teal and umber shadows, restrained paper grain, expressive natural faces, subtle imperfect painted edges. Human anatomy is believable, heads naturally sized; shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands, hips and knees belong to one continuous body. Seat hips on the actual seat, feet on the same floor, fingers visibly holding their actual objects; no disembodied hands, duplicated limbs, floating props or pasted-on heads. Keep important faces, hands, contact points and grounded figures within each wide panel with safe margins. Maintain the same identities, clothing, figure scale, prop design and spatial continuity across all six scenes. Anonymous original visual casting only, not likenesses of credited storytellers. This is a dramatic storyboard adaptation, not a claim that imagined symbols or staged details are verified events. Story: Fine. Palette accents: #D9D6C9, #4E6A76, #F3B89C. Identity continuity: SOLDIER: The same adult man with medium tan skin, short dark hair, muted olive service shirt with a few small anonymous medals, slate trousers and ordinary shoes; no identifiable unit insignia or battlefield wounds. THERAPIST: The same adult woman with warm brown skin, long dark brown hair, soft taupe blouse and slate skirt; professionally attentive without a white coat or diagnostic labels. FAMILY: An existing offscreen voice only. Do not invent or merge a visible family member with the therapist. TOP LEFT (frame 0): In a quiet orderly room, the soldier stands unnaturally straight beside a plain wooden chair, heels grounded and hands held too tightly together. Small medals are genuinely pinned to his olive shirt, one resting slightly askew. A compressed soft charcoal cloud above his head suggests restless nights without picturing combat or faces. His mouth is controlled, his eyes tired. The wall and floor remain ordinary, giving the rigid silhouette room to be read. TOP RIGHT (frame 1): The same man now sits on the edge of the home chair, feet flat, back still military straight, fingers interlocked over his knees. He glances away toward a dim doorway where the family voice comes from; no other person is shown. One shoulder has drawn defensively inward. The charcoal pressure shape has crowded closer to him, but there are no literal monsters or war scenes. His reassurance looks practiced and exhausting. MIDDLE LEFT (frame 2): A modest consultation room with two real chairs placed at an open angle and a low table with water, no barrier desk. The soldier sits braced in one chair; the therapist sits opposite at equal eye height, feet on the same floor and hands resting on her own lap. She leans only slightly forward and asks gently, leaving his personal space intact. His medals and clenched hands remain visible; the setting is human rather than clinical spectacle. MIDDLE RIGHT (frame 3): From a closer but still complete two-chair view, the soldier eases back enough that the chair actually supports his weight. His hands have unlinked, one palm resting on his thigh and the other releasing the chair arm. His shoulders lower unevenly and his eyes turn down. The therapist remains quietly present with her own hands still. The compressed graphite cloud has a small opening, not a vanishing cure. Keep chair legs and both people's grounded feet coherent. BOTTOM LEFT (frame 4): The soldier lifts his gaze toward the therapist with a vulnerable, searching expression, one hand turned a little upward near his knee rather than gesturing grandly. His other hand rests loosely. She receives the admission with a calm face and no consoling touch that he has not invited. The same chairs and small table fix their distance. Soft warm light reaches his face while the medals remain pinned and the night-colored cloud remains faintly present. BOTTOM RIGHT (frame 5): Widen slightly to both seated people sharing an ordinary breathing space. The therapist offers one small open hand over her own knee as she replies; the soldier's relaxed hands and newly level shoulders show he can hear her. The cloud's edge is open to room light, but its graphite traces and the small medals are still there. No triumphant transformation, embrace or suddenly carefree grin; simply two bodies supported by their chairs. Story-specific safeguards: Keep FAMILY offscreen and THERAPIST separate from family. Medals remain anonymous, physically pinned and present at the end. The charcoal shape is an explicitly visual metaphor; no supernatural event, graphic memory or instant therapeutic cure.
